newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy president urges clarity on separatist action.
newsitem.headline: Italy president urges clarity on separatist action.

text.p: Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro called on magistrates on Friday to clarify when separatist campaigners were acting legally and when they were breaking the law.
He said the boundaries of what constituted legal action were shifting and that he was "deeply concerned by a certain psychological climate" that tended to underestimate the actions of separatists.
"The Italian people have the right to know where the legal area ends and where illegality starts. There is no doubt that this is the task of the magistrature, which is free and independent," he said.
Scalfaro, who is from the northern city of Novara, has been a constant critic of the separatist drive for affluent northern Italy by the Northern League party and smaller movements.
Last Sunday, on the same day the League staged its own unofficial "referendum" for a separate state across the north, Scalfaro said Italy had to remain "one and indivisible".

On Friday, in his speech to an audience that included Prime Minister Romano Prodi, he said Italy's image and dignity was being damaged by separatist actions, including the occupation this month of Venice's bell tower by eight armed secessionists.
The secessionists, who were swiftly arrested, are now on trial on a string of charges that could put them in jail for more than 20 years in the event of conviction.

Scalfaro's speech, to mark Italy's annual police day, got a mixed response from magistrates and politicians, one of whom said the implicit suggestion that the state should crack down on separatism would play into the hands of the Northern League.

League leader Umberto Bossi, who has several court cases pending for alleged defamatory remarks against the Italian state, said Scalfaro wanted to "persecute the patriots of Padania", the name he has given to northern Italy.
"It seems to me that there is no more room for mediation after Scalfaro's speech. If this is the situation, the only way forward is to speed up the independence of Padania," Bossi said.
